title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase: +5.1% (to $4.56)
drivers.evidence: Sales dropped 42% (119) in a recent week at same price, vs baseline. Historical price sensitivity shows 22% volatility; this price point is outside normal range. No promotion, so no offset. Heatwave may increase demand, but price effect dominates.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is a significant, non-promotional price hike. Recent data shows a 22% drop in sales when price was last $4.56 (2026-09-28: 207 vs baseline, 2026-10-05: 119 vs baseline). The heatwave (38°C) is a known demand driver for dairy—sales typically rise in extreme heat. Historical data shows no direct heatwave effect, but the price spike is the dominant factor. The classical model suggests no uplift, but it ignores price sensitivity. The price increase likely reduces demand. Evidence supports a downward adjustment of ~15%. No promotion or event. The spread remains 1.0 due to strong price effect evidence.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
